chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a woman who performed Hajj with us while she was pregnant and had never performed Hajj before; she would be jostled until she touched the Stone. He said, 'Do not deceive her (by forcing her into the crowd).' I said, 'So is it excused for her?' He said, 'We used to say that it is necessary to touch it in the first of the seven circuits, then we saw that the people had increased and were eager (to touch it), so (it is no longer necessary).'

And I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who is carried in a litter, touches the Stone, and circumambulates the House without illness or excuse, and he said, 'I dislike that for her.'
As for her being carried so that she touches the Stone, due to the jostling of men, there is no objection to it, until when she has touched it, she circumambulates on foot.

And as for the Istihada woman (one with non-menstrual bleeding), there is no objection to her circumambulating the House and running between Safa and Marwa, if she does what the Istihada woman does. Narrated.
ai.seo_question: What are the Hajj rulings for pregnant women and those carried in litters regarding touching the Stone and circumambulation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the flexibility in Hajj rituals for pregnant women and those carried in litters, prioritizing safety from jostling (zihm) over the strict obligation of touching the Black Stone, reflecting the principle of removing hardship (raf' al-haraj). He further clarifies that while carrying to touch the stone is permissible to avoid crowding, the circumambulation itself should ideally be performed on foot, whereas women with Istihada are fully permitted to perform Tawaf and Sa'i, treating them similarly to menstruating women in terms of ritual purity exemptions. This narration highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on practical ease and the distinction between essential pillars and recommended acts during Hajj.
